name: Image Pool (slideshow)
description: Presentation shell for continuous narration over a slideshow of YOUR OWN still images. Defines HOW the video is built: a single continuous narration (no chapters) paired with images pulled randomly from an Image Pool in the B-Roll Library, each held for a configurable few seconds with a slow Ken-Burns motion and crossfades, plus burned-in subtitles. Scene Prompts / Scene Generator / Video Generator pages stay HIDDEN — there are no per-scene AI images, the Image Pool is the visual layer. Pipeline: idea → single continuous-narration script → audio → pick images (random, cross-episode no-repeat) → ffmpeg slideshow → final video. The niche layered on top sets the voice and subject. NOT for visually-driven per-scene storytelling (use Scenes), NOT for img2img character continuity (use Continuity), NOT for stock video clips (use Stock Footage).

idea.systemPromptRole: You are helping generate new episode ideas for a narration-led channel that pairs spoken word with a slideshow of still images. The niche layered on top (if any) sets the subject domain and voice.
idea.guidanceText: Each idea is a single continuous spoken piece paired with a calm image slideshow. The niche layer sets the topic domain and voice.

script.systemPromptRole: You are writing a single continuous narration (no chapters) for an audio-first channel paired with a slideshow of still images. The niche layer sets the voice and subject.
additionalRules: Write as continuous prose — no chapter headings, no list structure, no bullet points.
Pace for a slow, measured spoken delivery. Short sentences. Natural pauses.
Address the listener directly ('you', 'your'). Avoid third-person narrative distance.
End with a clear closing line that signals the listener should let the words settle.
pacingArc: Open with a single grounding line that invites the listener in.
Middle: cycle through several short reflections, each landing on a concrete image or phrase the listener can carry.
Close: a single sentence of release / dismissal.
script.closingHint: Single continuous narration block — no chapter splits.
